risks.title: Critical dependence on third-party manufacturers (Dalton)
risks.summary: Cardiol is highly dependent on Dalton Pharma Services and other CMOs for the manufacturing of its product candidates. Any service interruption, quality failure, or cost increase could delay clinical trials and commercialization. The lack of internal production capabilities exposes the company to supply chain risks.
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly cited in the forward-looking list ("dependence on Dalton and other contract manufacturers"). Direct language indicating major operational dependence. Lack of control over future production costs mentioned separately. Critical industrial category for clinical-stage biotech.

risks.title: Clinical uncertainty and risk of trial failure
risks.summary: Cardiol's commercial success depends entirely on the efficacy and safety of CardiolRx and other candidates in clinical trials (acute myocarditis, recurrent pericarditis, heart failure). Equivocal or negative results could destroy the company's value and block market access.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned 4 times in the forward-looking section ("inherent uncertainty of product development", "equivocal or negative results from clinical trials"). Very cautious language reflecting intrinsic uncertainty. Phase II ARCHER trial ongoing. Existential risk for a pre-commercialization biotech.

risks.title: Ongoing financing needs and cash burn
risks.summary: Cardiol has no commercial revenues and is burning cash to fund R&D and clinical trials. The company will need to raise additional capital, exposing shareholders to significant dilution. A closed capital market could paralyze operations.
risks.score_rationale: Cited first in forward-looking risks ("anticipated cash needs, and the need for additional financing"). Mentioned 3 times ("requirement for additional financing", "negative cash flow from operations", "history of losses"). Pre-revenue biotech with a history of losses. Risk of dilution or inability to fund.

risks.title: Intellectual property: risks related to enforcement and freedom to operate
risks.summary: Cardiol relies on patents to protect CardiolRx, its formulations, and administration routes. Risks include third-party challenges, patent invalidation, or unintentional infringement of third-party rights (notably via the Meros agreement). Lack of freedom to operate could block commercialization.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly listed ("ability to procure, defend, and/or enforce our intellectual property" and "freedom to operate"). Risk of third parties contesting ownership ("third-party claims relating to misappropriation"). Meros agreement with complex use fields. Critical for a biotech.

risks.title: Lack of commercial experience and market adoption risk
risks.summary: Cardiol has never commercialized a pharmaceutical product. The company will need to build a brand, sales force, and relationships with third-party payers. Market acceptance of CardiolRx in acute myocarditis and pericarditis remains uncertain, with risk of low adoption.
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly cited ("lack of experience in commercializing any products, including selling, marketing, or distributing"). Also "uncertainty relating to market acceptance of our product candidates". Biotech without commercial history. Risk of positioning and adoption.

risks.title: Regulation of controlled substances and jurisdictional variability
risks.summary: Cardiol's product candidates (especially cannabinoid-based ones via Meros) are subject to controlled substance laws (CDSA in Canada, CSA in the USA). Regulatory variations across jurisdictions complicate clinical development and future commercialization.
risks.score_rationale: Specifically mentioned ("product candidates being subject to controlled substance laws which may vary from jurisdiction to jurisdiction"). Cardiol is developing cannabinoids (Meros agreement). High multi-jurisdictional compliance risk.

risks.title: Product liability and personal injury claims
risks.summary: Once commercialized, CardiolRx and other products could generate civil liability claims for death or injury. Product recalls or litigation could damage reputation and result in significant uninsured costs.
risks.score_rationale: Cited twice ("claims for personal injury or death arising from the use of our products" and "product liability claims and product recalls"). Inherent risk in pharmaceutical products. Potential for insufficient insurance coverage.

risks.title: Intense competition and risk of technological obsolescence
risks.summary: Cardiol operates in a highly competitive sector dominated by established pharma companies. The emergence of new therapies (cellular, gene) or improvements in existing treatments could render CardiolRx obsolete or non-competitive in terms of price/efficacy.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned ("competition in our industry" and "inability to develop new technologies and products and the obsolescence of existing technologies"). Cardiovascular market is highly competitive with established players. Risk of technological disruption.

ai_positioning.summary: Cardiol Therapeutics does not mention AI or machine learning in its drug development or operations. The company focuses on traditional clinical research centered on CardiolRx (cannabidiol) for cardiovascular diseases.
